source.title_on_document: Brainstorming with a Generative Language Model: Effect of Exposure to AI Ideas on Brainstorming Performance and Cognitive Load

supplement.where: Online Appendices A-E, 'available online via http://link.springer.com'; 'The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12599-025-00974-y' (PDF p. 9, Sect. 3.3; PDF p. 22, end matter)
supplement.holds: A: user interaction with the app and information flow to and from the GLM; B: full explanation of the prompt template; C: full post-survey questionnaire; D: operationalization of all brainstorming performance metrics and variables; E: qualitative coding scheme. The main text does not say whether the appendices hold descriptive statistics (arm means, SDs, or arm sizes).

paper_design_summary: 75 university students (mostly informatics) were randomly assigned to brainstorm alone or with an embedded GPT-3.5 tool that supplied three ideas per click on demand, in a 10-minute session on 'How can we reduce food waste?'. Participants then shortlisted their four best ideas. Fluency and flexibility (categories covered) were counted per session, and novelty and value of shortlisted ideas were rated by five blind judges (and GPT-4), both for human-origin ideas only (human level) and for all ideas including copied GLM ideas (dyad level).

studies.label: Between-subjects experiment: human-only vs human + GLM brainstorming

assignment.what_was_assigned: Brainstorming app with the GLM idea function deactivated (human-only) versus activated (human + GLM)
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. In the human-only baseline, each person brainstormed individually with the app's GLM function deactivated.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1031), Sect. 3.2; Fig. 4 ('Random assignment to condition'); design described PDF p. 8 (p. 1030), Sect. 3.1

arms.name: human + GLM
arms.description: Brainstormed in the app with a right-side 'AI ideas' panel; each 'Generate ideas' click returned three GPT-3.5 ideas that could be copied into the participant's idea list; at least one request was required

arms.name: human-only
arms.description: Brainstormed alone in the same app with the GLM function deactivated

participants.exclusions: 77 participants brainstormed and completed the survey; 2 excluded: one who misunderstood the task (condition not stated) and one in the human + GLM condition who did not request any GLM ideas. For human-level novelty and value, four further human + GLM participants who shortlisted none of their own ideas were excluded from those two analyses (implying 71 people; the paper does not print 71). The paper does not give per-arm counts; the sensitivity analysis uses 'group sizes of 38 and 37' without naming which arm is which.
participants.who: University students, all but one in study programs at the informatics department; age mean 23.3 (18-37); 13 female, 62 male; experiment integrated into in-person university seminars across four courses
participants.country: not_stated (participants 'attend a Western European University'; authors at University of Hamburg, Germany)
participants.quote: 77 participants brainstormed and completed the survey. We excluded data from two participants ... Of the remaining 75 participants
participants.locator: PDF p. 10 (journal p. 1032), Sect. 3.4; group sizes PDF p. 12 (p. 1034), Sect. 3.6

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-3.5-turbo-0301, temperature 0.9, embedded in a purpose-built brainstorming app
ai_tool.how_used: Pull design: on each 'Generate ideas' click, the backend filled a fixed prompt template with the question, the participant's own idea list, and earlier GLM ideas, and returned three ideas of at most 20 words each; participants could copy GLM ideas into their long list. Participants did not write prompts.

task.description: Brainstorm as many ideas as possible (Osborn rules, wild ideas encouraged) on 'How can we reduce food waste?', then shortlist the four best ideas from the long list regardless of origin

outcomes.name: Dyad-level novelty of shortlisted ideas (dyad_novelty)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean novelty ('how novel, original or surprising the idea is', 7-point scale) of the participant's four shortlisted ideas, including GLM-origin ideas, rated by five blind-to-condition judges including three of the authors; ICC(C,k) = 0.864. Robustness: GPT-4 ratings of the shortlist; and a 'Good-Idea-Count' of long-list ideas above the average GPT-4 novelty rating.

contrasts.reported: human-only mean = 2.876 vs human + GLM mean = 3.396; Student's t(73) = 2.889, p = 0.005, Cohen's d = 0.667 (Fig. 8c interval plot). GPT-4-rated: U = 932.5, p = 0.015. Good-Idea-Count (novelty): U = 1073.5, p < 0.001; mdn human-only = 2, mdn human+GLM = 4. No SDs printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 13 (journal p. 1035), Sect. 4.2, Fig. 8c; GPT-4 and Good-Idea-Count PDF p. 14 (p. 1036), Sect. 4.2; Table 2 (PDF p. 15) H2-c

outcomes.name: Dyad-level value of shortlisted ideas (dyad_value)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean value ('how useful the idea is', 7-point scale) of the four shortlisted ideas including GLM-origin ideas, same five blind judges; ICC(C,k) = 0.736. Robustness: GPT-4 ratings; Good-Idea-Count of long-list ideas above the average GPT-4 value rating.

contrasts.reported: Mann-Whitney U = 994.0, p = 0.002, rB = 0.414; human-only mdn = 4.425 vs human + GLM mdn = 4.900 (Fig. 8d boxplot). GPT-4-rated: U = 986.5, p = 0.003. Good-Idea-Count (value): U = 1095.5, p < 0.001; mdn human-only = 2, mdn human+GLM = 6.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 13 (journal p. 1035), Sect. 4.2, Fig. 8d; GPT-4 and Good-Idea-Count PDF p. 14 (p. 1036); Table 2 (PDF p. 15) H2-d

outcomes.name: Dyad-level fluency (dyad_fluency, number of ideas in the long list including copied GLM ideas)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of ideas in the participant's long list, including GLM ideas the participant copied; GLM ideas not copied are not counted

contrasts.reported: human-only mdn = 5 vs human + GLM mdn = 7; Mann-Whitney U = 963.5, p = 0.006; rB = 0.371 (Fig. 8a boxplot)
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 13 (journal p. 1035), Sect. 4.2, Fig. 8a; Table 2 (PDF p. 15) H2-a

outcomes.name: Dyad-level flexibility (dyad_flexibility, number of categories covered including copied GLM ideas)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of categories (Specht et al. 2019 food-waste category system) with at least one idea in the session; ideas categorized by a blind-to-condition student assistant

contrasts.reported: human-only mdn = 3 vs human + GLM mdn = 5; Mann-Whitney U = 1080.0, p < 0.001; rB = 0.536 (Fig. 8b boxplot)
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 13 (journal p. 1035), Sect. 4.2, Fig. 8b; Table 2 (PDF p. 15) H2-b

outcomes.name: Human-level novelty of shortlisted human-origin ideas (human_novelty)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean judge-rated novelty of the participant's shortlisted ideas that originated from the participant (GLM ideas excluded); four human + GLM participants with no own idea on the shortlist excluded. Robustness: GPT-4 ratings; Good-Idea-Count on human-origin long-list ideas.

contrasts.reported: Mann-Whitney U = 699.5, p = 0.406 (Fig. 7c). GPT-4-rated: U = 757.0, p = 0.569. Good-Idea-Count (novelty, threshold mean = 3.396): U = 663.5, p = 0.672. No arm medians or means printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12-13 (journal p. 1034-1035), Sect. 4.1, Fig. 7c; Table 2 (PDF p. 15) H1-c

outcomes.name: Human-level value of shortlisted human-origin ideas (human_value)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean judge-rated value of the participant's own shortlisted ideas (GLM ideas excluded); same four exclusions as S1-O5. Robustness: GPT-4 ratings; Good-Idea-Count.

contrasts.reported: Mann-Whitney U = 737.5, p = 0.204 (Fig. 7d). GPT-4-rated: U = 653.5, p = 0.602. Good-Idea-Count (value, threshold mean = 4.747): U = 619.5, p = 0.369. No arm medians or means printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 13 (journal p. 1035), Sect. 4.1, Fig. 7d; Table 2 (PDF p. 15) H1-d

outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of ideas originating from the participant, GLM ideas excluded

contrasts.reported: human-only mdn = 5 vs human + GLM mdn = 4; Mann-Whitney U = 475.0, p = 0.015; rB = -0.324; 'corresponds to a Cohen's d = 0.581' (Fig. 7a)
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12 (journal p. 1034), Sect. 4.1, Fig. 7a (PDF p. 13); Table 2 (PDF p. 15) H1-a

outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of categories with at least one human-origin idea in the session

contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12 (journal p. 1034), Sect. 4.1, Fig. 7b (PDF p. 13); Table 2 (PDF p. 15) H1-b

company_involvement.description: Funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF), project HyMeKI (01IS20057); OpenAI models used as tools only

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly assigned to brainstorm with or without an embedded GPT-3.5 idea generator (PDF p. 9, Sect. 3.2); 75 people analyzed (PDF p. 10, Sect. 3.4), about 38 and 37 per arm (mapping not stated); outcomes are judge-rated novelty and value plus fluency and flexibility of the ideas produced. Human-level novelty and value analyses drop four more treatment participants (about 71 people), still above 50.

one_line_finding: With GPT-3.5 ideas available, the human + GLM dyads' shortlisted ideas were rated more novel (mean 3.396 vs 2.876; t(73) = 2.889, p = 0.005, d = 0.667) and more valuable (mdn 4.900 vs 4.425; U = 994.0, p = 0.002), and covered more categories, but participants' own ideas were fewer (mdn 4 vs 5; p = 0.015) and not more novel or valuable (PDF pp. 12-13, Sects. 4.1-4.2, Figs. 7-8).
open_questions: Design class: lab_rct chosen because sessions ran in person inside university seminars; the task (food-waste brainstorming) was not course content. A reviewer could argue field_rct ('integrated into in-person university seminars across four courses').

Rater type: novelty and value were rated by five blind judges including three of the authors; coded expert_raters, but they are researchers, not food-waste domain experts. human_raters is the alternative.

Per-arm counts are not printed. Sensitivity analysis uses group sizes 38 and 37; '6 participants (16.2%)' in the human + GLM responsibility question equals 6/37, which suggests human + GLM = 37 and human-only = 38, but the paper never states this.

Primary record choice: the paper gives hypotheses at two levels (human-only ideas vs dyad output including copied GLM ideas) and names no primary outcome. The dyad-level outcome is what the participant submitted with AI available; the human-level outcome isolates the participant's own ideas. Review should decide which level enters the pooled with_ai estimate.

The GPT-4 Good-Idea-Count threshold for novelty is printed as 'mean = 3.396', the same number as the dyad-level human + GLM judge-rated novelty mean (3.396). Possibly a coincidence or a typo; check against the online appendix.
No standard deviations are printed for any outcome; the online appendix (not in this PDF) may hold descriptives.
notes: Outcomes not listed: NASA-TLX cognitive load (self-report; t(73) = -0.892, p = 0.375, PDF p. 14, Fig. 9); self-reported cognitive stimulation and felt responsibility (self-report); and the exploratory comparison of GLM-origin vs human-origin shortlisted ideas (GLM ideas rated higher: novelty U = 9654.0, p < 0.001, mdn 4.0 vs 2.8; value U = 10,573.0, p < 0.001, mdn 5.2 vs 4.6; unit = 283 shortlisted ideas; PDF p. 14, Sect. 4.4), which compares AI output with human output inside the treatment arm and answers none of the three questions. No across-people diversity outcome is measured; the discussion mentions homogenization only as a question for future research (PDF p. 17). Totals: 373 ideas contributed, 206 GLM requests, 177 suggestions copied, 283 ideas shortlisted (224 human, 59 GLM) (PDF p. 12, Sect. 4). Sensitivity: detectable d >= 0.656 (t test) and >= 0.671 (Mann-Whitney) at 80 percent power (PDF p. 12, Sect. 3.6). PDF page N corresponds to journal page 1022 + N.
